Subject: FintechCo post-demo: performance SLO checklist & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time for yesterday’s demo. Per our discussion I pulled together a short SLO checklist and proposed MAP (mutual action plan) so we’re aligned on performance requirements and next steps. The attached spreadsheet has the checklist broken down by metric and test/validation owners. High-level items below: 

- Latency targets: p95 < 200ms for single-request generation (avg prompt length ~120 tokens); p99 < 400ms for capped tails.
- Throughput: baseline 500 requests/sec sustained for batch runs; peak burst to 1,500 rps for short periods (<= 5m).
- Concurrency: support 50 concurrent live streams without degradation (concurrency targets include 40 UI sessions + room for background jobs).
- Streaming: client requires chunked partial-response streaming for UX (first token within 80ms ideally).
- Accuracy/quality: we’ll track a sample set of 200 prompts from your production prompts for regression monitoring.
- Warmup & cold-starts: we recommend a warm pool with kept-alive contexts and KV cache priming; see notes in the attached PDF.

Attachments: fintechco_slo_checklist.xlsx, redwood_perf_summary.pdf

Next steps / proposed MAP: 
1) Engineering sync (Redwood infra + FintechCo eng) to review checklist and test plan — target week of Mar 27. (Owner: Rishi)
2) Provide access to a representative prompt set and a small testbed token feed — FintechCo to share by Mar 24. (Owner: Alex)
3) Redwood to provision staging environment with matching instance types and run baseline throughput/latency tests (3 days). (Owner: Neha)
4) Joint run: run streaming/latency test & collect traces; evaluate against p95/p99/streaming first-token SLA. (Owner: FintechCo + Redwood)

Please review the checklist and confirm anything missing or any constraints (region, data residency, encryption) we should bake into the staging runs. Happy to set the engineering call — available Tue/Thu next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligns with our internal expectations. A few quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Latency: is p95 measured end-to-end (client -> Redwood -> model) or just model-token latency? We need end-to-end numbers to include network.
2) Streaming: our UX team expects the first partial token within 100ms on average for standard desktop clients. You mentioned 80ms in the email — is 100ms a safer target for our initial rollout?
3) Throughput/concurrency: the 1,500 rps burst is from batch jobs. For interactive traffic, we expect 200-300 rps sustained with spikes. Can Redwood run tests separated by interactive vs batch so we can see isolation characteristics?

We can share an anonymized prompt set by Friday (Mar 24). Regarding the engineering sync, Thu Mar 29 morning PST works for our eng team.

—Alex

FintechCo

Alex — thanks for the fast reply and the great questions. Quick answers inline and a slightly adjusted checklist attached.

1) Latency measurement: we’ll report both model-side token latency (service -> model kernel) and end-to-end p95/p99 (client -> Redwood -> model -> client). For the joint run we’ll capture network latencies via client-side agents so you’ll get the full E2E numbers.

2) Streaming first-token: 100ms average first-token is reasonable as an initial rollout target; we’ll aim for 80ms as a stretch goal and include that in the success criteria.

3) Isolation for interactive vs batch: yes — our staging tests will include separate test buckets for interactive (sustained 300 rps, target p95 <200ms) and batch (burst to 1,500 rps, baseline throughput verification). We’ll provide both aggregated and per-bucket metrics.

Updated MAP items and owners: 
- Rishi (Redwood infra) to schedule and lead the engineering sync on Thu Mar 29 10:00 AM PST.
- Alex to share anonymized prompt set by Fri Mar 24.
- Neha to provision staging cluster and post test-capacity plan by Mon Mar 27.
- Joint run planned week of Apr 3 (3-day window) with an observations doc to follow.

If that timeline works I’ll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda (checklist review, test infra, data access, acceptance criteria). Confirm Thu Mar 29 10:00 AM PST or propose another slot.

Thanks — Marissa
